transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining me. As you know, we're reviewing the proposed eighth-grade makerspace program before I make a final authorization decision. The program would involve 24 students meeting twice weekly during the spring semester, using soldering stations, hand tools, and a laser cutter, with one STEM teacher supervising. I'd like to hear from each of you on the implementation details I routinely ask about before approving a new program. Let's start with you — what information can you share relevant to making this program safe and workable?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I completed my room-safety review this week, and it found two critical constraints: the makerspace may enroll no more than 16 students total, and any session using soldering stations with more than 12 students requires two supervising adults. The draft program form still shows the original numbers of 24 students and one supervising adult, so those will need to be revised before the program can be authorized.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I've completed my review of the participating students' health records, and I found one student with a documented severe nickel allergy. That student may only participate when the program uses nickel-free components, and I need to approve the materials list before each session. I should also note that this health-record review hasn't been added to the program file yet, so we'll need to make sure that happens.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I need to flag a technology compliance issue with the draft program. I confirmed with the district technology office that student design files for this equipment may not use cloud storage. The approved workflow requires an offline design workstation with files transferred by encrypted USB after an IT malware scan. However, the draft program currently still specifies cloud-based computer-aided design files, so that will need to be revised before authorization.
transcript.speaker: A4
